questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Constant Term For the Fourier Series
questions.problem:
$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{2}x)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{2}x)
$$

Let $F(x)=3{x}^{2}+2x$ for $x\in [-2,2).$ The Fourier series of the $4$-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the exact value of ${a}_{0}.$

${a}_{0}=$ {{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
For the Fourier series of a $2L$-periodic function, the constant term is given by

$$
{a}_{0}=\frac{1}{L}{\int }_{-L}^{L}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $L=2$ and $f(x)=3{x}^{2}+2x$ for $x\in [-2,2).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-2}^{2}(3{x}^{2}+2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{[{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}]}_{-2}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(({2}^{3}+{2}^{2})-((-2)^{3}+(-2)^{2})) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(12-(-4)) \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Constant Term For the Fourier Series
questions.problem:
$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2nx)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2nx)
$$

Let $F(x)=3{x}^{2}+4x$ for $x\in [-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}).$ The Fourier series of the $\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the exact value of ${a}_{0}.$

${a}_{0}=$ {{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
For the Fourier series of a $2L$-periodic function, the constant term is given by

$$
{a}_{0}=\frac{1}{L}{\int }_{-L}^{L}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $L=\frac{\pi }{2}$ and $f(x)=3{x}^{2}+4x$ for $x\in [-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}(3{x}^{2}+4x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }{[{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}]}_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }((\frac{{\pi }^{3}}{8}+\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{2})-(-\frac{{\pi }^{3}}{8}+\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{2})) \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }(\frac{{\pi }^{3}}{4}) \\  & =\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{4}x)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{4}x)
$$

Let $F(x)=5x-4$ for $x\in [-4,4).$ The Fourier series of the $8$-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the exact value of ${a}_{0}.$

${a}_{0}=$ {{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
For the Fourier series of a $2L$-periodic function, the constant term is given by

$$
{a}_{0}=\frac{1}{L}{\int }_{-L}^{L}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $L=4$ and $f(x)=5x-4$ for $x\in [-4,4).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{-4}^{4}(5x-4)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{[\frac{5}{2}{x}^{2}-4x]}_{-4}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}((\frac{5}{2}\cdot {4}^{2}-4\cdot 4)-(\frac{5}{2}\cdot (-4)^{2}-4\cdot (-4))) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(24-56) \\  & =-8.\end{aligned}
$$
